candidate.title: Feature-flag constant evaluates to raw encryption-key string instead of boolean, risking secret leakage
reports: [advisory] process.env.calcomwebhooksecret && process.env.calcomappcredentialencryptionkey evaluates to its last operand, so the exported appcredentialsharingenabled constant's value is the raw encryption key string, not a boolean. any code path that logs, serializes, or client-bundles this constant (constants.ts already mixes nextpublic client-facing values) leaks the credential encryption key; wrapping in boolean(...) makes it safe.

[advisory] appcredentialsharingenabled is defined as process.env.calcomwebhooksecret && process.env.calcomappcredentialencryptionkey, which evaluates to the raw aes encryption key string, not a boolean. a developer debugging credential sync who logs or serializes the flag-named constant (the natural move for an enabled flag) writes the credential encryption key into logs, and any future === true comparison silently reads the feature as disabled.

[bug] appcredentialsharingenabled is env && env, which evaluates to a string (or undefined), not a boolean; it is exported from a constants module full of boolean flags and consumed in boolean contexts. consumers get a truthy string (e.g. the secret value) wherever they expect true; any future use in a strict boolean context (zod boolean schema, a boolean api field, === true check) silently misfires, and the exported value leaks the raw secret string into anything that serializes the flag.
appcredentialsharingenabled is derived via process.env.x && process.env.y string truthiness, so setting a var to a non-empty but meaningless value like 'false' enables sharing

appcredentialsharingenabled uses truthy-string semantics (any non-empty string including 'false' enables it) instead of the codebase's === "1" convention, so self-hosters trying to disable the feature actually arm the webhook and sync-refresh paths with secret 'false'

appcredentialsharingenabled is not a boolean: a && b evaluates to the value of b, so the constant is typed string | undefined and holds the raw calcomappcredentialencryptionkey when enabled, leaking the secret if logged or serialized; it also omits calcomcredentialsyncendpoint so the real enablement condition is re-implemented and can drift in refreshoauthtokens.ts and parserefreshtokenresponse.ts
